summary: This note is a wiki-style overview of the Minnesota Golden Gophers football program, the University of Minnesota's team at the NCAA Division I FBS level. It covers the program's founding in 1882, its Big Ten Conference membership, and its claimed national championships. It also notes the home stadium since 2009 and the January 2017 change from head coach Tracy Claeys to P.J. Fleck.
one_line: Overview of the Minnesota Golden Gophers football program, covering its history, Big Ten membership, seven claimed national titles, home stadium, and 2017 coaching change.
key_facts: The Minnesota Golden Gophers football program represents the University of Minnesota in college football at the NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) level.
The Minnesota Golden Gophers football program was founded in 1882.
The Minnesota Golden Gophers football program is one of the oldest in college football.
Minnesota has been a member of the Big Ten Conference since its inception in 1896 as the Western Conference.
The Golden Gophers claim seven national championships.
The Golden Gophers' claimed national championships are from the years 1904, 1934, 1935, 1936, 1940, 1941, and 1960.
Since 2009, the Golden Gophers have played all their home games at TCF Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
In January 2017, the Minnesota Golden Gophers football program fired head coach Tracy Claeys.
In January 2017, the Minnesota Golden Gophers football program hired former Western Michigan head coach P.J. Fleck as its new head coach.
